[DOC_ID:task-model] Task model routing  
Open WebUI routes titles, tags, follow-up suggestions, retrieval queries, web-search queries, and autocomplete through the configured task model. Administrators can set a local or smaller task model without changing the main chat model.

[DOC_ID:task-cap] Task output limits  
The task.model.params dictionary applies generation parameters across task endpoints. A max_tokens cap therefore reaches titles and autocomplete as well as tags, follow-ups, and queries; it is not a narrow tag-only control.

[DOC_ID:autocomplete] Autocomplete workload  
Autocomplete is disabled by default at the server and user preference levels. When enabled, the editor waits 1000 milliseconds after an input change and checks cursor and loading state, so requests are not sent on every keystroke.

[DOC_ID:query-cache] Query reuse  
ENABLE_QUERIES_CACHE stores web-search queries on request state so later file retrieval in the same combined chat request can reuse them. Repeating the standalone query endpoint cannot exercise this optimization.

[DOC_ID:resume-cache] Paid output cache  
Cache every paid response under a stable key that binds condition, dataset hash, endpoint, and payload. Write the cache atomically before the append-only action manifest. On resume, a valid cache alone must prevent a repeated provider call.

[DOC_ID:wire-capture] Proxy evidence  
Capture redacted provider request and response bodies, actual reported input, output, and cached tokens, completion latency, and all budget mutations. For nonstreaming task calls, mark time to first token unavailable rather than relabeling response time.

[DOC_ID:rag-top-k] Retrieved chunk count  
The rag.top_k configuration defaults to three. Document and collection retrieval pass this value to vector or hybrid search unless a request-level k overrides it. Compare k values 3, 2, and 1 on one fixed indexed corpus.

[DOC_ID:quality] Targeted quality evaluation
